native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: Increasing education expenditure (% of GNI) is associated with a more favorable —roughly neutral instead of negative— level of per-capita GDP (GNI pc) in Sub-Saharan Africa than in developing (lower-middle-income) countries: the LMC main association is negative (beta ≈ -0.12 to -0.45 per pp of GNI) while the EduExp x SSA interaction is consistently positive across specifications (delta ≈ +0.15 to +0.61, p = 0.007-0.178), leaving an approximately zero net association in SSA. Associations only; SSA GNI observed solely 2011-2015; no imputation performed.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) wide->long->pivot melt to 82-row panel (2 groups x 41 years, 1975-2015); 2) descriptive statistics by group and window (means, ranges, linear trends, CAGR, peaks/troughs); 3) central pooled (unbalanced) regressions log(GNI_pc) ~ EduExp + SSA + EduExp x SSA with controls (secondary enrollment, exports growth, labor force participation), HAC/Newey-West SEs (no clustered SEs; 2 units), no SSA GNI imputation; 4) balanced 2011-2015 window robustness (n=10); 5) lagged EduExp (t-1, t-2) with lag x SSA interaction for endogeneity, plus dynamic spec with lagged log GNI; 6) auxiliary supportive analysis of secondary enrollment ~ education expenditure over 1975-2015 (n=41 per group); 7) declared limitations (associational only, denominator effect of %-of-GNI measure, low power).

sub_hypo.context: Developing countries outside versus within Sub-Saharan Africa.
sub_hypo.relations: Increasing education expenditure has a larger effect on per capita GDP in developing countries outside Sub-Saharan Africa than in those within it.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it

sub_hypo.text: Increasing education expenditure as a percentage of GNI is associated with a more favorable, approximately neutral level of per-capita GNI in Sub-Saharan Africa than in lower-middle-income countries, where the association is negative.
sub_hypo.context: Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) and lower-middle-income countries (LMC), using an unbalanced 1975–2015 panel. SSA GNI is observed only in 2011–2015, with no imputation; robustness analysis uses the balanced 2011–2015 window (n=10). Pooled regressions control for secondary enrollment, exports growth, and labor force participation, with HAC/Newey-West standard errors. Additional specifications include education expenditure lagged one and two years and its interactions with SSA, and lagged log GNI. Findings are associational only, with limitations from the percentage-of-GNI denominator and low power.
variables: Country Group / Country Code (SSA versus LMC)
Series Name: Adjusted savings: education expenditure (percentage of GNI)
Series Name: GNI per capita (constant 2015 US dollar), log-transformed in regressions
Series Name: School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross), control
Series Name: Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth), control
Series Name: Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate), control
sub_hypo.relations: In regressions of log GNI per capita, the LMC education-expenditure association is negative (beta approximately -0.12 to -0.45 per percentage point of GNI). The education expenditure × SSA interaction is consistently positive across specifications (delta approximately +0.15 to +0.61; p=0.007–0.178), leaving an approximately zero net association in SSA. These are associations, not causal effects.

Associations only; SSA GNI observed solely 2011-2015; no imputation performed.
